title: A Pune invoicing-fintech beat the 'never heard of you' objection with founder LinkedIn, not paid lead-gen
content: SITUATION: A Pune B2B fintech offering invoicing-plus-working-capital to SMEs was burning ₹3.2L/month on Google Search and Meta lead-gen. CPL looked fine at ₹480, but only 6% of demo requests converted to paid (target 18%), and calls stalled on one line: 'We've never heard of you — who's behind this?' In a category crowded with fly-by-night lending apps, the leak was trust, not traffic. ACTION: We cut paid by 60% (₹3.2L to ₹1.28L) and put the founder on LinkedIn — three posts a week: a Surat textile trader's blocked working capital, an honest teardown of why GST-linked invoice financing gets rejected, real underwriting decisions. A 2-minute YouTube explainer on invoice-discounting was embedded in posts and shared to existing customers via WhatsApp Status. OUTCOME: Over 14 weeks the founder grew 1,400 to 9,800 followers; inbound demos rose 41% at no incremental media cost (founder time aside). Demos arriving pre-sold from content converted at 21% vs 6% on cold paid; blended CAC fell ₹8,000 to ₹4,600. Two posts were named back to him on sales calls.
lesson: In low-trust B2B fintech, a buyer's first question is 'who's behind this' — no CPL optimisation answers it. Move budget from cold lead-gen into a named, specific founder voice (real customer failures and underwriting calls, not features), and let prospects self-qualify before the demo. Track demo-to-paid by source, not blended CPL: the content cohort converts 3x because it arrives pre-trusted. The catch is it's founder-time-intensive and compounds slowly — start before you're desperate.
